diffs.diff: pin count: part has 32 (INT RST GND 3V3 SDA SCL GND_2 0 1 2 3 VCC1 4 5 6 7 OSC RST_2 GND_3 3.3V SDA_2 SCL_2 8 9 10 11 VCC2 12 13 14 15 GND_4), datasheet reading has 27 (OSC RST GND 3.3V SDA SCL 7 6 5 4 VC1 3 2 1 0 GND 8 9 10 11 VC2 12 13 14 15 GND INT)
diffs.evidence: The SparkFun BOB-13601 silkscreen (hardware-top.jpg / hardware-input-headers-2.jpg) shows two complete 6-pin I2C/power headers: 'INT RST GND 3V3 SDA SCL' on one edge and 'OSC RST GND 3.3V SDA SCL' on the opposite edge. It also shows two 10-pin I/O columns: 'GND 0 1 2 3 VC1 4 5 6 7' and '8 9 10 11 VC2 12 13 14 15 GND'. That is 6+6+10+10 = 32 signal pads, matching the model. The hookup guide says 'These two headers at the top and bottom of the breakout board are the input and control headers' and 'The pairs of power and I2C pins are the only ones required'. The second reading has only 27 pins because it kept INT from the INT/RST/GND/3V3/SDA/SCL header but dropped that header's other five pins (RST, GND, 3V3, SDA, SCL). 'VC1/VC2' on the silkscreen is the same as the model's VCC1/VCC2, which the guide calls 'VCC1 and VCC2'. Neither reading counts the outer GND rail rows.
